C00000901.about: BUILD-PAC is the political action committee of the National Association of Home Builders, the trade association of home builders, remodelers and related businesses with more than 140,000 members. It gives to housing-friendly candidates for Congress in both parties.

C00000935.about: The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is the official campaign arm of Democrats in the U.S. House. It raises money, recruits and supports candidates, contributes to Democratic House campaigns, and runs independent-expenditure ads against Republicans in competitive districts.

C00001016.about: The Carpenters Legislative Improvement Committee is the political action committee of the United Brotherhood of Carpenters and Joiners of America, one of North America's largest building trades unions with more than half a million members. It supports federal candidates who back working people, infrastructure investment and fair trade, mainly through direct contributions to members of Congress.

C00002469.about: The Machinists Non-Partisan Political League is the political arm of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, the union representing machinists, aerospace, manufacturing and transportation workers. Created in 1947, it pools voluntary contributions from IAM members to back federal candidates who support the union's positions on trade, labor law, transportation and U.S. manufacturing. Its direct contributions go mostly to Democratic members of Congress.

C00002972.about: America's Electric Cooperatives PAC is the political action committee of the National Rural Electric Cooperative Association (NRECA), the Arlington, Virginia-based trade group for more than 900 not-for-profit, member-owned electric cooperatives serving over 40 million people, led by former Utah Rep. Jim Matheson. It gives directly to congressional candidates of both parties.

C00003251.about: The NEA Fund for Children and Public Education is the federal PAC of the National Education Association, the union of public school teachers and education employees. It makes direct contributions to congressional candidates, overwhelmingly Democrats.

C00004036.about: SEIU COPE is the federal political committee of the Service Employees International Union, a union of about 2 million workers in health care, public services and property services led by president April Verrett. Long one of the largest organizational donors in federal politics, it gives almost entirely to Democrats and also spends independently in Senate and House races, backing Democrats such as Raphael Warnock, John Fetterman and Jacky Rosen.

C00004275.about: BankPAC is the political action committee of the American Bankers Association, the Washington-based trade association that has lobbied for the U.S. banking industry since 1875 and is led by president and CEO Rob Nichols. It gives directly to House and Senate candidates of both parties.

C00005249.about: NAIFAPAC is the federal political action committee of the National Association of Insurance and Financial Advisors, the trade association for insurance agents and financial advisors. Founded by NAIFA's board in 1966, it is funded by pooled voluntary contributions from NAIFA members. It gives directly to federal candidates and national party committees on a nonpartisan basis, supporting Republicans and Democrats who back the industry's priorities.

C00007542.about: The SMART Political Action League is the federal PAC of the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART), an AFL-CIO union created by the merger of the Sheet Metal Workers International Association and the United Transportation Union. SMART represents sheet metal workers, service technicians, rail engineers and conductors, bus operators, welders and other workers across North America. The PAC gives directly to congressional candidates.

C00007880.about: America's Credit Unions PAC is the political action committee of America's Credit Unions, the national trade association for state- and federally chartered credit unions formed in 2024 by the merger of the Credit Union National Association and the National Association of Federally-Insured Credit Unions. It raises money from individuals in the credit union movement, working with participating credit unions and state leagues. It gives to pro-credit union candidates of both parties and makes independent expenditures for incumbents such as Young Kim, Vicente Gonzalez and Don Bacon.

C00007922.about: LIUNA PAC is the federal political action committee of the Laborers' International Union of North America, a construction and public-service union founded in 1903 with about half a million members in the United States and Canada, led by general president Brent Booker. It gives directly to congressional candidates.

C00010868.about: ACEC/PAC is the political action committee of the American Council of Engineering Companies, the business association of engineering and design firms. Established in 1975 and overseen by engineering firm executives, it is the largest federal PAC in the design industry. It gives to members of Congress of both parties who back a pro-business and infrastructure agenda.

C00011114.about: AFSCME PEOPLE (Public Employees Organized to Promote Legislative Equality) is the federal political action committee of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees, the AFL-CIO union for public service workers. It is funded by voluntary political contributions from union members, pooled to back pro-labor candidates. It gives directly to candidates, overwhelmingly Democrats, and makes independent expenditures supporting allies and opposing Republican challengers in Senate and House races.

C00012245.about: UBS PAC is the political action committee of UBS Americas, the U.S. arm of Swiss banking giant UBS Group, the world's largest private bank and wealth manager. It gives directly to congressional candidates of both parties.

C00022343.about: InsurPac is the federal political action committee of the Independent Insurance Agents & Brokers of America, known as the Big "I", the trade association for independent insurance agencies. Established in 1974, it is funded by personal, LLC and partnership contributions from independent agents, brokers, carrier executives and association staff; corporate money is not accepted. It gives directly to federal candidates who support independent agents and uses fundraising events to connect Big "I" lobbyists and agents with members of Congress.

C00023580.about: The Letter Carrier Political Fund, formerly the Committee on Letter Carrier Political Education, is the political action committee of the National Association of Letter Carriers, the AFL-CIO union representing city letter carriers of the U.S. Postal Service. It is funded by voluntary contributions from members, since union dues cannot be used for federal campaigns. It gives directly to candidates of both parties who support letter carrier jobs and the Postal Service.

C00024521.about: AAJ PAC is the political action committee of the American Association for Justice, the national trade association of plaintiffs' trial lawyers, formerly the Association of Trial Lawyers of America. It is funded by individual lawyer members, law firms and affiliated state trial lawyer associations. It gives to federal candidates who support access to the civil courts, overwhelmingly Democrats.

C00024968.about: AOA-PAC is the political action committee of the American Optometric Association, the professional group for doctors of optometry. It gives direct contributions to members of Congress in both parties.

C00027342.about: The IBEW Political Action Committee is the federal PAC of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, the union representing workers in construction, utilities, telecommunications, broadcasting, manufacturing and railroads. It makes direct contributions to candidates, almost all of them Democrats.

C00027466.about: The National Republican Senatorial Committee is the official campaign arm of Republicans in the U.S. Senate. It raises money, recruits Senate candidates, contributes to Republican campaigns, and runs coordinated and independent ads against Democratic senators and candidates in battleground states.

C00028860.about: AFT Committee on Political Education is the federal political action committee of the American Federation of Teachers, the AFL-CIO union that is the second-largest teachers union in the United States. It gives directly to congressional candidates.

C00029447.about: FIREPAC is the political action committee of the International Association of Fire Fighters, the AFL-CIO union representing paid professional firefighters and emergency medical personnel in the United States and Canada. It gives directly to congressional candidates of both parties.

C00029504.about: The Engineers Political Education Committee is the federal PAC of the International Union of Operating Engineers, the AFL-CIO construction union representing heavy equipment operators, mechanics, surveyors and stationary engineers in the United States and Canada. It gives directly to congressional candidates of both parties and has made independent expenditures supporting Democrats such as John Fetterman.

C00030718.about: The Realtors Political Action Committee (RPAC) is the federal PAC of the National Association of Realtors, the trade association for real estate agents and brokers. Funded by voluntary contributions from Realtor members rather than dues, it gives directly to candidates of both parties and also makes independent expenditures. It picks candidates based on voting records, its candidate questionnaire and positions on homeownership and real estate investment.

C00035451.about: ALPA-PAC is the political action committee of the Air Line Pilots Association, the world's largest pilots union, representing about 80,000 pilots at U.S. and Canadian airlines. It gives to members of Congress of both parties.

C00039578.about: CouncilPAC is the political action committee of The Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers, the Washington trade association for commercial insurance and employee benefits brokerages. Funded by voluntary contributions from employees of its member firms, it is the insurance industry's largest PAC. It gives directly to members of Congress of both parties, with priorities including tax policy, flood insurance and pharmacy benefit manager transparency.

C00040998.about: NADA PAC is the political action committee of the National Automobile Dealers Association, the Tysons, Virginia, trade group founded in 1917 that represents franchised new car and truck dealerships before Congress and federal agencies. Formerly called the Dealers Election Action Committee, it gives directly to House and Senate candidates.

C00042366.about: The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee is the official campaign arm of Democrats in the U.S. Senate. It raises money, recruits Senate candidates, contributes to Democratic campaigns, and runs coordinated and independent ads against Republican senators and candidates in battleground states.

C00053553.about: The NRA Political Victory Fund is the political action committee of the National Rifle Association, founded in 1976. It grades candidates from A+ to F on gun rights, endorses candidates, contributes directly to their campaigns, and runs independent ads and voter mobilization. Its support goes overwhelmingly to Republicans, including House GOP leaders and Republican Senate challengers, and it spends against Democratic senators in battleground states.

C00064766.about: UPSPAC is the employee-funded political action committee of United Parcel Service, the Atlanta-based package delivery and logistics company. It gives to candidates of both parties, favoring lawmakers who represent areas with large UPS workforces or facilities and who sit on committees important to the company's business.

C00075820.about: The National Republican Congressional Committee is the official campaign arm of Republicans in the U.S. House. It raises money, recruits candidates, contributes to Republican House campaigns, and runs independent-expenditure ads against Democratic members and candidates in competitive districts.

C00077321.about: AICPA PAC is the federal political action committee of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, the national professional association of CPAs. Established in 1977 and funded by voluntary personal contributions from members, it gives to congressional candidates of both parties who support the accounting profession.

C00078451.about: The General Dynamics Employee PAC is the political action committee of General Dynamics, the Reston, Virginia-based aerospace and defense contractor that builds submarines, combat vehicles and Gulfstream jets. The corporation itself makes no political contributions; the PAC is funded by voluntary donations from eligible U.S. employees. It gives to members of both parties, favoring those who support national security and aerospace, represent areas with General Dynamics facilities or employees, or sit on key committees, and it does not give to presidential campaigns or super PACs.

C00096156.about: HONPAC is the political action committee of Honeywell International, the industrial and aerospace technology company. It is funded only by voluntary contributions from eligible U.S. Honeywell employees, since the company does not use corporate funds for political contributions. It describes itself as bipartisan and gives to members of Congress of both parties.

C00097568.about: RTX PAC is the employee political action committee of RTX Corporation, the aerospace and defense company formerly known as Raytheon Technologies, whose businesses are Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney and Raytheon. It is funded by voluntary employee contributions rather than corporate money and is governed by a steering committee of company leaders. It gives directly to candidates of both parties, weighing their support for the military, intelligence and civil aviation programs and their ties to RTX facilities, with defense appropriators and Armed Services Committee leaders among its top recipients.

C00106146.about: The American Hospital Association PAC is the political action committee of the American Hospital Association, the Chicago-based trade group representing nearly 5,000 hospitals and health care providers. It gives direct contributions to members of Congress from both parties and also runs independent ads supporting incumbents of both parties. Its giving backs the association's lobbying on Medicare payments and other hospital issues.

C00107235.about: The PricewaterhouseCoopers PAC is the political action committee of PwC US, the accounting, tax and consulting firm. It gives directly to congressional candidates of both parties, with tax writers and Financial Services Committee members among its leading recipients. The firm has said the PAC is bipartisan and has made a point of directing more of its money to women candidates.

C00109017.about: The AT&T Employee Federal PAC is the political action committee of AT&T, the telecommunications company. It gives to members of Congress of both parties.

C00110338.about: The American Crystal Sugar Company PAC is the political action committee of American Crystal Sugar, a Moorhead, Minnesota, cooperative owned by sugarbeet growers in the Red River Valley of Minnesota and North Dakota and the largest beet sugar producer in the U.S. The PAC gives directly to House and Senate candidates of both parties and to sugar industry PACs such as the U.S. Beet Sugar Association's.

C00127811.about: U.S. Israel PAC (USI PAC) is a pro-Israel political action committee based in Hollywood, Florida, registered with the FEC since 1980. It is funded by individual donors and makes direct contributions to congressional candidates of both parties who support the U.S.-Israel relationship.

C00130773.about: NMHC PAC is the political action committee of the National Multifamily Housing Council, the trade association of the apartment industry. Formed in 1980 and funded by individual contributions from industry members, it supports federal candidates of both parties who favor the production and preservation of multifamily housing.

C00142711.about: The Boeing Company PAC is the political action committee of Boeing, the Arlington, Virginia-based aerospace and defense manufacturer. It gives direct contributions to candidates and party committees of both parties.

C00144766.about: The NBWA PAC is the political action committee of the National Beer Wholesalers Association, the Alexandria, Virginia-based trade group for America's independent beer distributors. It is the largest PAC in the licensed beverage industry and gives direct contributions to members of Congress from both parties in roughly equal measure. Its giving supports the association's push to preserve the state-based system of alcohol regulation.

C00158881.about: The New York Life Insurance Company PAC is the political action committee of New York Life, the large mutual life insurance company. It gives direct contributions to candidates of both parties.

C00173153.about: CRNA-PAC is the political action committee of the American Association of Nurse Anesthesiology (formerly the American Association of Nurse Anesthetists), the professional association for certified registered nurse anesthetists, based in Rosemont, Illinois. It gives direct contributions to candidates of both parties and also runs independent digital and mail campaigns supporting House and Senate candidates.

C00211318.about: The Deloitte Political Action Committee is the PAC of Deloitte, the professional services firm specializing in audit, tax and consulting. It gives direct contributions to candidates and committees of both parties.

C00227744.about: The Ernst & Young Political Action Committee is the PAC of EY, the professional services firm specializing in audit, tax and consulting. It gives direct contributions to candidates and committees of both parties.

C00236489.about: KochPAC is the corporate political action committee of Koch, Inc. (Koch Industries), the Wichita, Kansas-based conglomerate whose businesses include Georgia-Pacific, Flint Hills Resources, Guardian Industries, Molex and Infor. It is funded by voluntary contributions from employees of Koch and its affiliates. The PAC gives directly to congressional candidates and party-aligned committees, overwhelmingly Republicans, with a small share going to Democrats.

C00238725.about: NATCA PAC is the political action committee of the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, the AFL-CIO union that represents the Federal Aviation Administration's air traffic controllers and other aviation safety workers. It gives to members of Congress of both parties.

C00248716.about: The Comcast Corporation & NBCUniversal PAC is the federal political action committee of Comcast, the Philadelphia-based cable, broadband and media conglomerate that owns NBCUniversal. It gives directly to congressional candidates of both parties.

C00284885.about: The Home Depot PAC is the employee-funded political action committee of The Home Depot, the home improvement retailer. It pools voluntary contributions from the company's salaried associates and gives to candidates and party committees on both sides of the aisle.

C00303024.about: The Lockheed Martin Employees' Political Action Committee (LMEPAC) is the PAC of Lockheed Martin, the aerospace and defense contractor, funded by voluntary contributions from eligible employees and directors. It gives to candidates and party committees of both parties, generally backing lawmakers who support national defense and the company's business priorities.

C00341396.about: MoveOn.org Political Action is the federal PAC of MoveOn, the progressive advocacy group founded in 1998 by Joan Blades and Wes Boyd, and is led by executive director Katie Bethell. It raises money largely from small online donors and both contributes directly to progressive Democrats such as Summer Lee, Maxwell Frost and Ilhan Omar and spends independently for Democratic Senate candidates and against Republicans.

C00345132.about: RJC PAC is the political action committee of the Republican Jewish Coalition, a Washington-based group founded in 1985 that connects Jewish Americans with Republican lawmakers and is led by executive director Matt Brooks and chairman Norm Coleman. It endorses Republican Senate and House candidates, both incumbents and challengers, who emphasize support for the U.S.-Israel alliance and opposition to antisemitism. Donors can give to the PAC's general fund or bundle contributions directly to endorsed candidates.

C00365536.about: CHC BOLD PAC is the campaign arm of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, founded in 2001 to increase Latino representation in Congress and chaired by Rep. Linda Sánchez. It gives to Latino Democrats and other Democrats in competitive races and runs independent expenditures on ads, plus RUIDO, a program of Latino content creators that mobilizes voters.

C00418897.about: VoteVets is a progressive veterans' political organization founded in 2006 by Iraq War veterans Jon Soltz and Jeremy Broussard. Its PAC endorses and funds Democratic candidates, especially military veterans running for Congress, through direct contributions, and runs ads supporting them and attacking Republican opponents in Senate and House races.

C00426775.about: The Charter Communications PAC is the employee political action committee of Charter Communications, the cable, broadband and phone company that sells service under the Spectrum brand. It gives direct contributions to candidates of both parties.

C00441949.about: JStreetPAC is the political action committee of J Street, the liberal pro-Israel, pro-peace advocacy group founded by Jeremy Ben-Ami. It endorses House and Senate candidates who back J Street's agenda, almost all of them Democrats, and channels members' donations directly to their campaigns. It also hosts events connecting members with candidates and officials.

C00448696.about: The Senate Conservatives Fund is a conservative Republican PAC founded in 2008 by then-Sen. Jim DeMint of South Carolina. It backs hard-line conservatives for the U.S. Senate, including primary challengers to sitting Republicans, by giving to their campaigns and running independent ads, mail, and email and text campaigns. It also spends against Democratic senators and Senate candidates in general elections.

C00467431.about: The Eye of the Tiger PAC is the leadership PAC of Louisiana Rep. Steve Scalise, a member of House Republican leadership. It is funded mostly by transfers from the Scalise Leadership Fund, his joint fundraising committee, along with contributions from other PACs. It gives the bulk of its money directly to Republican House candidates and incumbents.

C00473918.about: Women Vote! is the super PAC that serves as the independent expenditure arm of EMILY's List, the national group that works to elect Democratic women who support abortion rights. It is funded mainly by EMILY's List and major Democratic donors such as Irwin Jacobs, and it runs TV and digital ads, direct mail and research-driven persuasion campaigns aimed at women voters. It spends in Democratic primaries for EMILY's List-endorsed women as well as in general elections for Senate and House seats.

C00484642.about: Senate Majority PAC is the main super PAC working to elect Democrats to the U.S. Senate, aligned with Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and led by J.B. Poersch, a former executive director of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. Much of its money comes from its affiliated nonprofit Majority Forward, and it funds spinoff super PACs such as WinSenate and Last Best Place PAC. It reserves television and digital ad time in battleground Senate races to support Democratic candidates and attack Republicans.

C00486845.about: LCV Victory Fund is the super PAC of the League of Conservation Voters, the national environmental advocacy group known for its congressional scorecard and "Dirty Dozen" list. The League's own nonprofit arm is its largest funder. It spends on advertising and voter outreach to elect Democrats who back climate and environmental policy and to defeat Republicans in Senate, House and presidential races.

C00487363.about: American Crossroads is a Republican super PAC founded in 2010 by Karl Rove and former RNC chair Ed Gillespie and led by Steven Law. It is closely tied to Senate Leadership Fund and the nonprofit One Nation, and Senate Leadership Fund supplied much of its money in 2024. It runs television ads attacking Democratic Senate candidates in battleground states, often in joint reservations with Senate Leadership Fund.

C00487470.about: Club for Growth Action is the super PAC arm of the Club for Growth, the anti-tax conservative group led by former Indiana congressman David McIntosh. Its money comes largely from Susquehanna International Group co-founder Jeff Yass, with Richard Uihlein among other major donors. It runs ads backing limited-government conservatives, often intervening in Republican primaries, and attacks Democrats in general elections.

C00488742.about: The National Association of Realtors Congressional Fund is the super PAC of the National Association of Realtors, the trade association for real estate agents and brokers. It is funded through member dues and contributions from industry allies such as multiple listing services. It runs independent ad campaigns supporting incumbents and candidates of both parties, such as Republicans Chuck Grassley and David Valadao and Democrat Sherrod Brown.

C00489799.about: Planned Parenthood Votes is the super PAC of Planned Parenthood's political arm, working alongside the Planned Parenthood Action Fund and its federal PAC. It is funded by large individual donors, including members of the Soros family and Michael Bloomberg. It spends on ads and voter outreach supporting candidates who back abortion rights, almost always Democrats, and opposing Republicans in competitive Senate and House races.

C00489856.about: ESAFund, formerly the Ending Spending Action Fund, is a conservative super PAC founded in 2010 by TD Ameritrade founder Joe Ricketts to back candidates who favor balanced budgets and smaller government. The Ricketts family, led by Marlene Ricketts, is its main funder, and it works alongside an affiliated nonprofit, Ending Spending Inc. It runs ads supporting Republicans, notably Nebraska Sen. Deb Fischer, and opposing Democrats in Senate and House races.

C00490375.about: National Nurses United for Patient Protection is the super PAC of National Nurses United, the largest union of registered nurses in the United States and an AFL-CIO affiliate. It is funded by the union and its California Nurses Association affiliate. It supports progressive Democrats who back the union's priorities, such as Medicare for All and safe staffing ratios, mainly by paying union staff to canvass voters.

C00492140.about: American Bridge 21st Century (AB PAC) is a Democratic super PAC and opposition research group founded in 2010 by David Brock. It tracks and films Republican candidates, publishes research on them and runs large ad campaigns against Republicans in Senate, House and presidential races. Its funders include wealthy Democratic donors such as Reid Hoffman, Stephen Mandel and George Marcus, along with labor unions.

C00495028.about: House Majority PAC is the main super PAC devoted to electing Democrats to the U.S. House, aligned with House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries and led by former Nancy Pelosi aide Mike Smith. It works alongside the nonprofit House Majority Forward, and its donors have included Michael Bloomberg, J.B. Pritzker, Tom Steyer and Reid Hoffman. It reserves large blocks of television and digital advertising to defend Democratic incumbents and attack Republicans in battleground districts, and it has also recruited candidates and spent in competitive Democratic primaries.

C00495861.about: Priorities USA Action is a Democratic hybrid super PAC founded in 2011 by former Obama White House aides Bill Burton and Sean Sweeney to support Barack Obama's reelection, and later the main outside group backing Hillary Clinton and Joe Biden. Its major donors have included Donald Sussman, George Soros, James Simons, Haim and Cheryl Saban and Michael Bloomberg, and it is led by executive director Danielle Butterfield. It concentrates on digital advertising and voter-mobilization programs in battleground states for Democratic presidential, Senate and House candidates.

C00504530.about: Congressional Leadership Fund is the main super PAC dedicated to electing Republicans to the U.S. House, aligned with House GOP leadership and Speaker Mike Johnson. It shares its board with its sister nonprofit, the American Action Network, and its largest donors have included Ken Griffin, Patrick Ryan and Sheldon and Miriam Adelson. Most of its money goes to television and streaming ads in competitive House districts, defending vulnerable Republican incumbents and attacking Democratic challengers, along with small direct contributions to GOP candidates.

C00528554.about: The RJC Victory Fund is the super PAC affiliated with the Republican Jewish Coalition, the Washington-based group of Jewish Republicans chaired by former Sen. Norm Coleman and run by executive director Matt Brooks. It runs ads supporting Republican candidates in GOP primaries and general elections and opposing Democrats in competitive races. In 2026 it spent about $3.9 million to help Ed Gallrein defeat Rep. Thomas Massie in Kentucky's Republican primary.

C00530766.about: Women Speak Out PAC is the super PAC partner of SBA Pro-Life America, the anti-abortion group led by Marjorie Dannenfelser. It backs Republicans who oppose abortion and attacks Democrats over abortion rights in Senate, House and governor races, running a large door-to-door canvassing program alongside digital and video ads, texts, calls and mail. In 2024 it worked to elect Bernie Moreno, David McCormick and Tim Sheehy, and its 2026 ads target Democrats including Jon Ossoff and James Talarico.

C00532630.about: Our American Century is a Republican super PAC based in McLean, Virginia, founded in 2012 as Geaux PAC and renamed in 2017. Its major donors have included pharmaceutical entrepreneur Fred Eshelman, Texas oilman Tim Dunn, casino developer Steve Wynn, and Donald Trump's leadership PAC, Save America. It ran ads backing Trump in 2020 and, in later cycles, ads supporting Republican Senate and House candidates and attacking Democratic senators.

C00540203.about: Defending Main Street is the super PAC of the Republican Main Street Partnership, a group of center-right Republican members of Congress, and was founded in 2012 by former Ohio Rep. Steve LaTourette. It defends Republican incumbents in competitive districts and backs its preferred candidates in open seats and GOP primaries, using polling, digital ads and direct mail. In general elections it spends against Democratic challengers in swing House districts.

C00540443.about: Giffords PAC is the political committee of Giffords, the gun violence prevention organization led by former U.S. Rep. Gabby Giffords and her husband, Sen. Mark Kelly. It works to elect candidates who support gun safety measures such as universal background checks, endorsing candidates, giving to their campaigns, and running independent ads. It mostly backs Democrats, including House and Senate leaders, while spending against Republicans in competitive House districts, and has also supported some Republicans.

C00542217.about: Texans for a Conservative Majority is a Republican super PAC that backed Sen. John Cornyn in his 2026 primary and runoff against Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton. Its top donors include the nonprofits Ohio Works Inc. and America Works Fund, Houston businessman John Nau III, Blackstone CEO Stephen Schwarzman, Jim and Rob Walton, Sen. Pete Ricketts and Harlan Crow, and it has close ties to Trump adviser Chris LaCivita. It made multiple seven-figure TV buys attacking Paxton over his ethics record and also spent against Rep. Wesley Hunt.

C00550970.about: Equality PAC is the political arm of the Congressional Equality Caucus, the House caucus of LGBTQ members and allies, and is co-chaired by Reps. Ritchie Torres and Mark Takano. It works to elect LGBTQ candidates and allies who back the Equality Act, giving directly to Democratic campaigns and spending independently to boost LGBTQ candidates such as Scott Wiener, Julie Johnson and Emily Randall.

C00552851.about: The Freedom Caucus Fund is the campaign arm of the House Freedom Caucus, the bloc of hard-line conservative House Republicans; it operated as the House Freedom Fund until 2026. Retired donor Michael Rydin is by far its largest contributor in the 2026 cycle. It endorses and gives directly to conservative House candidates, including in Republican primaries, and runs ad campaigns backing caucus members such as Scott Perry, Lauren Boebert, Eli Crane and Nick Begich while attacking their Democratic opponents.

C00568444.about: Center Forward Committee is the super PAC of Center Forward, a centrist advocacy nonprofit that grew out of the Blue Dog Research Forum and is chaired by former Alabama Democratic Rep. Bud Cramer. Its money comes largely from Center Forward and the Blue Dog Coalition's PAC. It spends on mail and digital ads backing moderate Democrats such as Angie Craig, Haley Stevens and Josh Gottheimer, including in primaries, and attacking Republicans in swing House districts.

C00571588.about: Restoration of America PAC (formerly Restoration PAC) is a conservative super PAC founded in 2015 and led by Doug Truax, founder and CEO of the Restoration of America organization. Uline chief executive Richard Uihlein is by far its largest donor. It runs television and digital ads against Democrats, including Kamala Harris and Joe Biden in presidential races and Senate and House Democrats such as Tammy Baldwin and Jared Golden, and also funds other conservative groups and Republican Senate candidates.

C00571703.about: Senate Leadership Fund is the principal super PAC working to elect Republicans to the U.S. Senate. Allies of Mitch McConnell founded it in 2015, and it is now aligned with Majority Leader John Thune; its sister nonprofit One Nation and donors such as Ken Griffin, Paul Singer, Miriam Adelson and Stephen Schwarzman supply much of its money. It spends mainly on television and digital advertising in battleground Senate general elections, attacking Democratic candidates and boosting Republican nominees.

C00573261.about: End Citizens United is a Washington-based Democratic political action committee founded in 2015 to overturn the Supreme Court's Citizens United decision and curb big money in politics. It is led by president Tiffany Muller, who also runs its affiliate Let America Vote, and it raises most of its money from small grassroots donors. The group endorses Democrats who back campaign finance reform and refuse corporate PAC money, gives directly to their campaigns, and runs independent ads in competitive Senate and House races against Republicans.

C00580068.about: Progressive Turnout Project is a Chicago-based Democratic political committee that runs large-scale voter contact programs, describing itself as the largest such operation in the country; it is led by president Alex Morgan. It funds door-to-door canvassing, mail and digital outreach to turn out Democratic voters, mainly for House and Senate candidates in competitive races, and also contributes directly to Democratic candidates.

C00606962.about: Working Families Party PAC is the federal political committee of the Working Families Party, a progressive party founded in New York in 1998 by labor unions and community groups and led by national director Maurice Mitchell. It backs progressive Democrats in primaries and general elections with direct contributions and independent spending on canvassing, texting, phone banking, mail, digital and TV ads. In 2024 it spent to back Kamala Harris and Democratic Senate and House candidates, defend Summer Lee and Cori Bush, and oppose Wesley Bell in Missouri.

C00608943.about: ClearPath Action Fund is a super PAC founded by North Carolina businessman Jay Faison, its largest donor, to elect Republicans who back a conservative clean energy agenda. It is part of the ClearPath network, alongside the ClearPath Foundation and the advocacy group ClearPath Action. Each cycle it names a slate of Republican clean energy champions in Senate and House races, such as Lisa Murkowski, Bill Cassidy and Dan Newhouse, and backs them with TV, digital, radio and mail advertising.

C00609388.about: BlackPAC is a Washington, D.C.-based super PAC that works to mobilize Black voters for Democratic candidates. It was founded in 2016 by Adrianne Shropshire, its executive director, and was incubated by the Service Employees International Union, which has been a leading funder along with progressive committees and nonprofits such as Senate Majority PAC, Majority Forward and Priorities USA Action. It runs year-round voter contact in battleground states, including door-to-door canvassing, mail and digital outreach, and has backed Senate Democrats such as Raphael Warnock, John Fetterman and Elissa Slotkin.

C00620971.about: For Our Future is a progressive super PAC created in 2016 by Tom Steyer's NextGen Climate together with the AFL-CIO, AFSCME, the American Federation of Teachers and the National Education Association, which supplied most of its early funding. It runs field programs in battleground states, combining door-to-door canvassing with mail, phone calls and texts to turn out infrequent Democratic-leaning voters. It has backed Democratic Senate candidates in states such as Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin.

C00625533.about: New American Jobs Fund is a super PAC created in 2016 by the League of Conservation Voters Victory Fund and the United Steelworkers' USW Works, joining environmental and labor interests to elect Democrats to the Senate. Its money comes from those two founding groups. It spends on voter persuasion and turnout, including canvassing and texting, and has repeatedly backed Democrat Sherrod Brown and other Ohio Democrats.

C00630665.about: Justice Democrats is a progressive political action committee founded in 2017 by Bernie Sanders campaign veterans Saikat Chakrabarti and Zack Exley, among others, and led by executive director Alexandra Rojas. It recruits and backs insurgent candidates, mostly in Democratic primaries against incumbents, who refuse corporate PAC and lobbyist money; it helped elect Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ayanna Pressley, Summer Lee and Delia Ramirez. In 2026 it spent for primary challengers including Donavan McKinney against Rep. Shri Thanedar and Darializa Avila Chevalier against Rep. Adriano Espaillat.

C00633248.about: 314 Action Fund is the political arm of 314 Action, a group founded in 2016 by chemist and former congressional candidate Shaughnessy Naughton to elect Democrats with backgrounds in science, technology, engineering, math and medicine. It backs only Democrats, endorsing candidates, giving to their campaigns, and running independent ads in both primaries and general elections, such as its 2024 spending for Maxine Dexter in Oregon. It also spends against Republican House incumbents in competitive districts.

C00634261.about: Defend US PAC is a Republican super PAC based in Arlington, Virginia, active since 2017. Its money comes mostly from nonprofit groups, including American Prosperity Caucus, America Works Fund, American Exceptionalism Institute, Prosperity Alliance and American Advancement. It relies mainly on direct mail against Democratic Senate and House candidates, such as James Talarico in Texas and Catherine Cortez Masto in Nevada, and has backed Republicans including Markwayne Mullin and Ken Paxton.

C00657866.about: Protect Freedom PAC is a libertarian-leaning Republican super PAC created in 2017 by political advisers to Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky. Nearly all of its money comes from billionaire investor Jeff Yass. It backs Paul-aligned conservatives such as Thomas Massie, Mike Lee and Ron Johnson, often in Republican primaries, through media buys, get-out-the-vote work and transfers to allied super PACs, and attacks rival Republicans as well as Democrats.

C00662221.about: House Freedom Action is a super PAC aligned with the House Freedom Caucus, the bloc of hard-right House Republicans, and works alongside the caucus's political arm, the House Freedom Fund. It spends on ads and mail in Republican primaries for conservative candidates and in general elections to protect caucus members, such as its spending for Rep. Scott Perry and against his Democratic challenger Janelle Stelson in Pennsylvania.

C00666388.about: Duty and Country is a Democratic super PAC affiliated with Senate Majority PAC, the main outside group working to elect Democratic senators. Most of its money has come from the Democratic group Majority Forward, and entertainment executive Haim Saban gave in 2026. It focuses on Ohio Senate races: in the 2024 Republican primary it ran TV ads highlighting Bernie Moreno's conservative positions and Trump's endorsement to boost him as Sherrod Brown's opponent, and in 2026 it runs TV and digital ads against Republican Jon Husted to help Brown.

C00668905.about: American Patriots PAC is a Republican super PAC funded mainly by Citadel founder Ken Griffin and Elliott Investment Management's Paul Singer. It intervenes in Republican primaries, as when it ran ads backing John McGuire's 2024 challenge to House Freedom Caucus chair Bob Good in Virginia, and it buys TV and media ads against Democrats such as Eugene Vindman in competitive races.

C00685719.about: The DLGA PAC is the federal political committee of the Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association, a Washington-based group of Democratic state and territorial lieutenant governors re-founded in 2018. The association works to elect Democratic lieutenant governors and runs a program backing its members when they seek higher office. In 2026 it supported Lt. Govs. Juliana Stratton of Illinois and Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota in their U.S. Senate primaries, running an in-house direct mail and polling program for Stratton.

C00687103.about: Americans for Prosperity Action is the super PAC of Americans for Prosperity, the conservative advocacy network founded with backing from Charles and David Koch and led by CEO Emily Seidel; it also operates as CVA Action and LIBRE Action. It backs Republican candidates in Senate and House races, endorsing candidates such as Jon Husted in Ohio and John Sununu in New Hampshire. Its work combines digital and television advertising with a large paid door-to-door canvassing program in battleground states.

C00688655.about: Everytown for Gun Safety Victory Fund is the super PAC of Everytown for Gun Safety, the gun-violence-prevention organization Michael Bloomberg founded in 2014 to counter the National Rifle Association. Bloomberg is its main funder, alongside donors such as Steve Ballmer and Daniel Pritzker. It spends on TV, digital and mail advertising to elect Democrats who support gun safety laws and to defeat Republicans aligned with the gun lobby in Senate and House races.

C00693838.about: More Jobs, Less Government is a Republican super PAC focused on Montana's U.S. Senate races. In 2024 it was the largest outside spender in the state's Senate contest, paying for TV, radio, digital, mail and text campaigns for Tim Sheehy and against Democratic Sen. Jon Tester. In 2026 it has spent against Democratic Senate candidates in Montana; its donors include Blackstone CEO Stephen Schwarzman and coal executive Wayne Boich.

C00707844.about: EDF Action Votes is the super PAC affiliated with EDF Action, the political advocacy partner of the Environmental Defense Fund. It runs TV, digital and Spanish-language ad campaigns for candidates it sees as climate allies, mostly Democrats such as Jacky Rosen and Mark Kelly along with some Republicans such as Brian Fitzpatrick, and against candidates it opposes on environmental and energy policy. It has run ads alongside campaigns by the League of Conservation Voters Victory Fund.

C00710848.about: DMFI PAC is the political arm of Democratic Majority for Israel, a group founded in 2019 by Democratic pollster Mark Mellman to keep the Democratic Party pro-Israel; former Hoyer aide Brian Romick now leads it. It gives to pro-Israel Democrats and spends heavily in Democratic primaries, backing Shontel Brown against Nina Turner and helping George Latimer and Wesley Bell unseat Jamaal Bowman and Cori Bush in 2024. Its major donors have included Stacy Schusterman and Gary Lauder.

C00724203.about: Somos PAC is the political arm of Somos Votantes, a progressive Latino voter organization led by Melissa Morales. It has drawn funding from Democratic groups including Senate Majority PAC, Priorities USA and the League of Conservation Voters, along with political nonprofits. It runs door-to-door canvassing and bilingual ads and mail to turn out Latino voters for Democratic Senate and House candidates in states such as Arizona, Nevada and Texas.

C00733352.about: Americans 4 Security PAC is a Wisconsin-based Republican super PAC funded mainly by its affiliated nonprofit, Americans 4 Security Inc., with Conservative Americans PAC and Palantir CEO Alex Karp among its other large donors. It backs Republicans tied to defense spending, such as Appropriations chair Tom Cole and Rep. Ken Calvert, and Wisconsin House candidate Michael Alfonso. In 2026 it spent millions on ads attacking Rep. Young Kim in her California primary against Calvert.

C00739771.about: Unite to Win is a Washington-based super PAC active in 2026 Democratic Senate primaries, with its money routed through a single donor committee, Democracy Matters. It spent heavily on ads backing Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary against Abdul El-Sayed, and ran ads opposing Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota's Democratic Senate primary.

C00741710.about: NRA Victory Fund is the super PAC of the National Rifle Association, separate from the NRA's traditional Political Victory Fund PAC. It buys TV, digital and radio ads backing Republican Senate candidates and attacking Democrats, including Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff in Georgia, John Fetterman in Pennsylvania and Mark Kelly in Arizona.

C00744920.about: CFFE PAC is the political action committee of the Campaign for a Family Friendly Economy, an advocacy group pushing for affordable caregiving, health care and paid family leave. Its major donors include Melinda French Gates's Pivotal Ventures and the Opportunity Action Fund. It spends mainly to support Democrats in Senate and House races, including Sherrod Brown, Troy Jackson and James Talarico, through ads and field organizing, and against Republicans such as Susan Collins and Ron Johnson.

C00748475.about: Conservative Outsider PAC is a super PAC funded by Club for Growth Action, the political arm of the anti-tax Club for Growth. It buys TV ads in Republican primaries against candidates the Club opposes, including Katie Britt in Alabama's 2022 Senate primary, Pat McCrory in North Carolina, Mike Carey in Ohio and John McGuire in Virginia.

C00749085.about: The American Policy Fund is an Austin, Texas-based Republican super PAC that backed businessman Joe O'Dea in Colorado's 2022 U.S. Senate race. Its largest donor was banking heir Timothy Mellon, followed by the Senate Leadership Fund and hedge fund founder Paul Singer. It ran ads supporting O'Dea and attacking Democratic Sen. Michael Bennet.

C00750182.about: The Opportunity Matters Fund is a Republican super PAC aligned with South Carolina Sen. Tim Scott, built around his "opportunity agenda" of school choice, opportunity zones and economic mobility. Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison supplied most of its money, with Ben Navarro and Club for Growth Action among its other large donors. It spent on Senate races to help Republicans such as Ted Budd, Ron Johnson and Scott himself, and against Georgia Democrat Raphael Warnock.

C00752691.about: One for All Committee is a Dallas-based Democratic super PAC that focuses on persuading moderate women to vote for Democratic candidates. Its major donors include Karla Jurvetson, Reid Hoffman, the George Soros-funded Democracy PAC, the Sixteen Thirty Fund and the American Federation of Teachers. It spends mainly on digital advertising in presidential and Senate races, backing Democrats such as Kamala Harris, Tammy Baldwin, Elissa Slotkin and Mary Peltola.

C00754051.about: Workers Vote is a New York-based super PAC, originally named Take Back 2020, run by political staff of the hospitality workers union UNITE HERE and funded by UNITE HERE's PAC along with allied progressive groups. It supports Democrats almost entirely through field work: paid door-to-door canvassing, door hangers, mail and get-out-the-vote ads. Its largest efforts have been in Georgia, Nevada and Pennsylvania, backing Raphael Warnock, Jon Ossoff, Catherine Cortez Masto, John Fetterman and Nevada's House Democrats, often alongside the Culinary Workers Union Local 226.

C00760124.about: National Victory Action Fund is a Republican hybrid PAC formed in 2020 by GOP strategists and chaired by former Colorado Sen. Cory Gardner, with former RNC chief of staff Jeff Larson on its board. Its early funding came largely from Citadel founder Ken Griffin, along with Paul Singer and other Republican committees. It runs ads that steer supporters to donate directly to Republican Senate and House candidates' campaigns, mostly incumbents, and also contributes to candidates directly.

C00763193.about: Georgia Honor is a super PAC that Senate Majority PAC, the main outside group of Senate Democrats, set up for Georgia Senate runoffs; Senate Majority PAC is its sole funder and treasurer Rebecca Lambe oversees both. In the 2020-21 special-election runoff it ran ads against Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler and for Raphael Warnock. It returned for the December 2022 runoff, spending on TV ads backing Warnock and attacking Republican Herschel Walker.

C00769232.about: Jefferson Rising is a conservative super PAC funded overwhelmingly by Tim Dunn, the oil executive who runs CrownQuest Operating. In 2024 it bought TV and media ads against Democratic senators and Senate candidates, including Tammy Baldwin, Ruben Gallego, Jacky Rosen, Jon Tester and Martin Heinrich. It has also given money to other Republican super PACs, including Fight for Kentucky.

C00776385.about: Save Missouri Values is a super PAC formed to support Eric Schmitt's 2022 campaign for U.S. Senate in Missouri. Its donors included the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, the CEO of St. Louis-based World Wide Technology, and Prime Inc. CEO Robert Low. It ran cable and broadcast ads promoting Schmitt in the Republican primary, spent heavily attacking primary rival Vicky Hartzler, and later ran ads against Democrat Trudy Busch Valentine in the general election.

C00777185.about: Saving Arizona PAC is a Republican super PAC seeded with $10 million from tech billionaire Peter Thiel to support his protege Blake Masters in Arizona's 2022 U.S. Senate race. Thiel ultimately put about $15 million into the group, which ran TV ads that helped Masters win the Republican primary. After a pause, it returned in the general election without Thiel's money, running millions in ads attacking Democratic Sen. Mark Kelly, who won re-election.

C00786830.about: WelcomePAC is a centrist Democratic PAC co-founded by strategists Liam Kerr and Lauren Harper Pope that recruits and backs pragmatic Democrats in Republican-leaning and swing House districts. Its donors have included Reid Hoffman, Michael Bloomberg and members of the Walton family. It contributes directly to candidates such as Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and Jared Golden and buys TV and digital ads supporting its picks and opposing Republicans such as Nick LaLota.

C00789339.about: 34N22 is a Republican super PAC created in 2021 to back Herschel Walker's 2022 Senate campaign in Georgia; the name pairs Walker's University of Georgia jersey number with the election year. Home Depot co-founder Bernie Marcus and shipping-supplies magnate Richard Uihlein were among its largest donors. It ran digital, TV and billboard ads casting Democratic Sen. Raphael Warnock as a rubber stamp for President Biden.

C00790923.about: Buckeye Leadership Fund is a super PAC formed to back state Sen. Matt Dolan in Ohio's Republican Senate primaries in 2022 and 2024. It was funded largely by Dolan's parents, Cleveland Guardians owners Larry and Eva Dolan, along with the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and donors such as retail executive Leslie Wexner. In the 2024 primary it ran statewide TV and radio ads attacking Dolan's rivals Bernie Moreno and Frank LaRose.

C00792259.about: Put Utah First PAC was a super PAC formed in 2021 to back independent Evan McMullin's 2022 challenge to Republican Sen. Mike Lee of Utah, with former Arizona state senator and SkyMall founder Bob Worsley as treasurer. Its largest donor was Divvy co-founder Blake Murray, and other backers included LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, Rob Walton and members of the Cumming family. Most of its money paid for TV, digital and mail ads attacking Lee and tying him to Donald Trump, with a smaller share promoting McMullin.

C00792333.about: Progress Pinellas is a super PAC formed in November 2021 to spend in the race for Florida's 13th Congressional District in Pinellas County. Its funder is Chicago private equity investor Justin Ishbia, a founding partner of Shore Capital Partners. It ran negative TV ads and mailers against Republican Anna Paulina Luna, along with ads supporting Democrat Eric Lynn.

C00793869.about: Alaskans for L.I.S.A. (Leadership in a Strong Alaska) is a super PAC formed to support Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski's 2022 reelection. It is run by Murkowski allies including her former chief of staff Mike Pawlowski, former legislator Jerry Mackie, consultant Jim Lottsfeldt and attorney Scott Kendall, and its largest donor was Citadel founder Ken Griffin, with James and Kathryn Murdoch also among its backers. It spent on TV and digital ads promoting Murkowski and attacking her Trump-endorsed Republican challenger, Kelly Tshibaka.

C00794396.about: School Freedom Fund is a super PAC affiliated with Club for Growth Action, the political arm of the conservative Club for Growth that campaigns for school choice and private-school vouchers. Its money comes mainly from billionaire trader Jeff Yass of Susquehanna International Group, with Uline founder Richard Uihlein also a major donor. It runs TV ads in Republican primaries and general elections, backing conservatives and attacking opponents of school choice, and also spends heavily in state legislative primaries.

C00794891.about: American Leadership Action is a Republican super PAC formed in November 2021 to support Mehmet Oz in Pennsylvania's 2022 U.S. Senate race, directed by attorney John Fogarty with GOP strategist Larry McCarthy handling its media. Donald Trump's Save America PAC was among its contributors. It ran ads attacking David McCormick in the Republican primary and John Fetterman in the general election.

C00796045.about: Truth and Courage PAC is an Austin-based super PAC formed in December 2021 to keep Republican Ted Cruz in the U.S. Senate. It owns Cruz's podcast, The Verdict with Ted Cruz, and collects advertising royalties from its distributor iHeartMedia; casino owner Miriam Adelson gave it $1 million in 2024. It pays for door-knocking, phone banking and TV and streaming ads backing Cruz, and in 2026 ran English- and Spanish-language ads attacking his Democratic challenger James Talarico.

C00797670.about: AIPAC PAC is the political action committee of the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, the pro-Israel lobbying organization, which set it up in late 2021 after decades of not funding candidates itself. It gave capped direct contributions to House and Senate candidates of both parties whom AIPAC judged supportive of Israel, while its affiliated super PAC, United Democracy Project, handles unlimited outside spending. In 2026 AIPAC moved to end the PAC's direct contributions and endorsements and leave electoral work to United Democracy Project.

C00798116.about: Honor Pennsylvania is a super PAC formed in late 2021 to back Republican David McCormick's 2022 bid for the U.S. Senate in Pennsylvania. Citadel founder Ken Griffin supplied most of its initial money. It spent heavily on TV ads attacking McCormick's main primary rival, Mehmet Oz, as insufficiently conservative.

C00799031.about: United Democracy Project is a super PAC created in 2021 by AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, to spend directly in federal elections. Its major donors include Paul Singer, Marc Rowan and Haim Saban. It spends mostly in Democratic House primaries to elect candidates it considers pro-Israel and defeat critics of Israel, and has also spent in Senate primaries, such as against Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, and against Republican Rep. Thomas Massie in Kentucky.

C00801514.about: Protect Our Future PAC is a Democratic hybrid PAC launched in 2022 to elect candidates focused on pandemic prevention, led by president Michael Sadowsky. It was funded overwhelmingly by FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried, with additional money from FTX executive Nishad Singh. It spent in Democratic House primaries on TV, radio and digital ads, backing candidates such as Lucy McBath, Valerie Foushee and Carrick Flynn and attacking Andrea Salinas in Oregon.

C00804104.about: Wisconsin Truth PAC is a Republican super PAC formed in 2022 to help Sen. Ron Johnson win re-election in Wisconsin. Its money came mainly from a handful of wealthy donors, led by ABC Supply founder Diane Hendricks, banking heir Timothy Mellon, Uline owners Richard and Elizabeth Uihlein, and TD Ameritrade founder Joe Ricketts. It spent almost all of its funds on TV ads promoting Johnson and attacking his Democratic opponent, Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes.

C00804187.about: Web3 Forward is a crypto-industry super PAC that backs Democratic candidates it sees as friendly to the digital-asset industry. Its money came from GMI PAC, a crypto super PAC whose donors included FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried and venture investors Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz. In the 2022 Democratic primaries it ran ads for House candidates including Jasmine Crockett in Texas, Val Hoyle in Oregon and Patrick Branco in Hawaii.

C00809020.about: American Dream Federal Action is a Republican hybrid PAC launched in 2022 by Ryan Salame, then co-CEO of the cryptocurrency firm FTX Digital Markets, who was its sole individual funder. In the 2022 cycle it spent heavily on TV ads and direct mail supporting Republican House and Senate candidates in GOP primaries and general elections, including Katie Britt in Alabama. It has been largely inactive since that cycle.

C00811166.about: Sentinel Action Fund is a conservative super PAC launched in 2022 by Heritage Action for America, the political arm of the Heritage Foundation, and led by former Heritage Action executive director Jessica Anderson. It backs conservative Republicans in Senate and House races through volunteer door-knocking and voter outreach as well as television ad buys.

C00815753.about: J Street Action Fund is the super PAC of J Street, the liberal pro-Israel, pro-peace advocacy group founded by Jeremy Ben-Ami that supports a two-state solution. It runs independent ad campaigns in Democratic primaries and general elections, backing candidates aligned with J Street and opposing candidates supported by AIPAC. In 2026 it announced a $3 million ad campaign against five AIPAC-backed Republican House members, the largest super PAC effort in J Street's history.

C00817536.about: Climate Power Action is an environmental super PAC launched in 2022 as an offshoot of Climate Power, the climate advocacy group started in 2020 by Democratic strategist John Podesta. The League of Conservation Voters Victory Fund supplied most of its early money. It runs ads supporting Democrats who back climate policy, concentrating on reelecting incumbents in close Senate races, and has also opposed Republicans such as Wisconsin Sen. Ron Johnson.

C00819664.about: Evergreen Principles PAC was a Republican super PAC active in Washington's 2022 U.S. Senate race, where it backed Republican Tiffany Smiley against Democratic Sen. Patty Murray. Its major funder was the Senate Leadership Fund, the super PAC aligned with Senate Republican leader Mitch McConnell. It spent mostly on TV and digital ads attacking Murray, along with ads promoting Smiley.

C00825091.about: Vote Alaska Before Party is an Anchorage-based Democratic-aligned super PAC that backed Mary Peltola in her races for Alaska's at-large U.S. House seat. Its funding came largely from House Majority PAC, the main super PAC of House Democrats. It ran ads opposing Republican Nick Begich in the 2022 and 2024 House elections.

C00825851.about: Make America Great Again Inc. (MAGA Inc.) is the main super PAC supporting Donald Trump, registered in 2022 and seeded with money from Trump's Save America leadership PAC. Its leadership has included Trump advisers Taylor Budowich, Chris LaCivita and pollster Tony Fabrizio, and its biggest donors include Timothy Mellon, Jeff Yass, Kelcy Warren, Miriam Adelson and Greg and Anna Brockman. It funds ads backing Trump and his agenda, and in Senate races it has spent against Democrats such as Raphael Warnock, John Fetterman and Mark Kelly.

C00828533.about: Worker Power PAC for Georgia is a Democratic-aligned super PAC set up as the Georgia arm of Worker Power PAC, which runs canvassing programs in coalition with the hospitality workers union UNITE HERE Local 11. It was funded by transfers from Worker Power PAC and paid door-to-door canvassers to turn out voters for Sen. Raphael Warnock in his December 2022 runoff against Herschel Walker.

C00831404.about: With Honor Fund II is the super PAC of With Honor, a cross-partisan organization co-founded by Rye Barcott, David Gergen and Peter Dixon to elect more military veterans to Congress. It succeeded the original With Honor Fund, whose donors included Jeff Bezos, the Walton family and Michael Bloomberg, and received a large transfer from that committee. It backs veterans of both parties who sign a pledge of integrity, civility and cross-partisan work, running TV and digital ads for candidates such as Democrat Jared Golden and Republican Don Bacon.

C00834630.about: Buckeye Values PAC is a Republican super PAC that backed Bernie Moreno in Ohio's 2024 U.S. Senate race. During the GOP primary it ran TV ads and mailers attacking Moreno's rival Frank LaRose as too liberal, and it spent against Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown in the general election. Its donors include Protect Freedom PAC and NHA Action.

C00835959.about: Fairshake is the cryptocurrency industry's main super PAC, formed in 2023 and funded chiefly by Coinbase, Ripple Labs, Jump Trading and Andreessen Horowitz co-founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz. It backs pro-crypto candidates of both parties and opposes industry critics, spending in primaries and general elections; its affiliates Defend American Jobs and Protect Progress handle Republican and Democratic races respectively.

C00835967.about: Conservatives for American Excellence is a Republican super PAC registered in 2023 that spends in GOP primaries for the House and Senate. Its early funding came largely from Citadel founder Ken Griffin and Arkansas investment banker Warren Stephens. It runs TV ads and direct mail for and against Republican candidates, including attacks on Robert Onder in Missouri and Barry Moore in Alabama.

C00836221.about: Defend American Jobs is the Republican-side affiliate of Fairshake, the cryptocurrency industry's super PAC network, whose largest funders are Coinbase, Ripple Labs, Jump Trading and Andreessen Horowitz co-founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz. It runs ads supporting pro-crypto Republicans and opposing critics of the industry, spending most heavily against Sherrod Brown in Ohio's Senate races while backing Bernie Moreno and Jon Husted.

C00844530.about: Rolling Sea Action Fund is a Democratic hybrid PAC launched in 2023 by allies of the Congressional Black Caucus, with the long-range goal of electing the first Black Speaker of the House. It is led by Niccara Campbell-Wallace, former political director of the CBC PAC. The group mobilizes Black voters in competitive House districts through advertising, in-person organizing and community engagement, and also spends in Democratic primaries.

C00844613.about: Win It Back PAC is a conservative super PAC affiliated with Club for Growth Action and headed by Club for Growth president David McIntosh, with the Club's chief financial officer as treasurer. It launched in 2023 to oppose Donald Trump's nomination, then turned to attack ads against Democratic Senate and House candidates such as Ruben Gallego and Jacky Rosen. It also spends in Republican primaries, including ads against Rep. Andy Barr in Kentucky's 2026 Senate primary.

C00848440.about: Protect Progress is the Democratic-side affiliate of Fairshake, the cryptocurrency industry's super PAC network, funded mainly by Coinbase, Ripple Labs, Jump Trading and Andreessen Horowitz co-founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz. It runs ads backing pro-crypto Democrats such as Elissa Slotkin, Ruben Gallego and Christian Menefee, and spends in Democratic primaries against candidates seen as hostile to the industry, including Al Green and Oliver Gilbert.

C00849489.about: Keystone Renewal PAC is a Republican super PAC created in 2023 to elect Dave McCormick to the U.S. Senate from Pennsylvania. Its largest donors were Wall Street figures including Citadel CEO Ken Griffin, Elliott Management president Paul Singer and Susquehanna International Group co-founder Jeff Yass. It reserved tens of millions of dollars in Pennsylvania TV time for ads promoting McCormick and attacking Democratic Sen. Bob Casey.

C00849729.about: Last Best Place PAC is a Democratic super PAC created by Senate Majority PAC, the super PAC aligned with Chuck Schumer, which with its nonprofit affiliate Majority Forward supplied its money. It ran television ads attacking Republican Tim Sheehy in Montana's 2024 Senate race, beginning during the Republican primary, targeting his business record and finances.

C00853861.about: The Great Lakes Conservative Fund (GLCF) is a Michigan super PAC dedicated to electing Republican Mike Rogers to the U.S. Senate, led by Republican strategist Andy Surabian. Texas oil executive Tim Dunn of CrownQuest Operating is its largest donor, followed by Ken Griffin and Stephen Schwarzman. It spent heavily on ads for Rogers in 2024 against Democrat Elissa Slotkin and returned in 2026 against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.

C00854299.about: Bold America is a Democratic super PAC launched in 2023 by three former Congressional Hispanic Caucus members: New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham and former Reps. Lucille Roybal-Allard and Filemon Vela. It aims to increase Latino representation in Congress by protecting Hispanic Caucus incumbents and turning out Latino voters, with major 2026 money from United Democracy Project, Proximo Action, United Futures PAC and Democrats 2026. It runs TV ads in Democratic primaries and general elections, including a multimillion-dollar push for caucus chair Adriano Espaillat in his New York primary that mostly attacked challenger Darializa Avila Chevalier.

C00855064.about: Conservative Values for Utah is a super PAC formed in October 2023 to back Republican John Curtis for the U.S. Senate seat being vacated by Mitt Romney, endorsing him before he entered the race. Its largest donor is clean-energy conservative Jay Faison, and Walmart heir Robert Walton also gave. It was the top outside spender in the 2024 Utah Senate race, running ads for Curtis and against his primary rival Trent Staggs.

C00859355.about: Battleground New York is a Democratic super PAC focused on door-to-door canvassing in New York's competitive U.S. House districts. It is funded by a coalition of labor unions and progressive groups including 1199SEIU, 32BJ SEIU, AFSCME, CWA, the New York State Nurses Association, the Working Families Party, Indivisible and Planned Parenthood. It works to defend Democrats such as Laura Gillen and Josh Riley and to unseat Republicans including Mike Lawler.

C00859660.about: New Democrat Majority is a super PAC aligned with the New Democrat Coalition, the House bloc of centrist, business-friendly Democrats, whose Action Fund has given it money. Most of its funding comes from the nonprofit groups Opportunity Forward Alliance and Effective Governing Coalition. It buys TV ads in Democratic primaries, backing centrist candidates such as Ben McAdams in Utah, Melissa Bean in Illinois and Cait Conley in New York and opposing progressives such as Rep. Cori Bush.

C00864926.about: America Leads Action is a Republican super PAC that spends in GOP House primaries against candidates aligned with or endorsed by the hard-right House Freedom Caucus, such as Mark Harris and Brandon Gill in 2024, while backing more establishment-minded Republicans. It has been largely funded by SnapAV founder Jay Faison and Walmart heir Rob Walton.

C00865444.about: WinSenate is a Democratic super PAC that serves as an affiliate of Senate Majority PAC, the super PAC aligned with Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, which supplies nearly all of its money. It runs television and digital ad campaigns in Senate general elections, attacking Republican candidates and incumbents in battleground states such as Ohio, Maine, North Carolina, Iowa and New Hampshire.

C00870030.about: Maryland's Future is a Republican super PAC formed to support former Gov. Larry Hogan in Maryland's 2024 U.S. Senate race. Its donors included Citadel founder Ken Griffin, Blackstone chief Stephen Schwarzman and his wife Christine, and Harlan Crow. It spent almost entirely on television ads attacking Democrat Angela Alsobrooks.

C00870592.about: Fix Washington PAC is a Republican-aligned super PAC created in February 2024 to defeat Democratic Sen. Tammy Baldwin of Wisconsin. Its main funder was Steven Hovde, chairman of Hovde Properties and brother of Republican Senate nominee Eric Hovde. It spent almost entirely on digital and broadcast ad campaigns attacking Baldwin during the 2024 race.

C00871368.about: Project 218 is a Democratic super PAC formed in 2024 and run by staff of American Bridge 21st Century, the Democratic opposition-research and advertising group. It is funded by wealthy Democratic donors and allied groups, including Democracy Matters, Amy Rao and Russell Siegelman. It runs television ads supporting Democratic House candidates in competitive districts, such as Josh Riley, Susan Wild and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, and also funds other Democratic groups.

C00872085.about: South Carolina Patriots PAC is a super PAC formed in 2024 that was funded entirely by a group called America Fund. It spent in the 2024 Republican primary for South Carolina's 1st District, running TV, digital and canvassing campaigns against Representative Nancy Mace and supporting her challenger Catherine Templeton.

C00875278.about: Last Frontier PAC is a Republican super PAC, registered in 2024, that backs Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska. In the 2026 U.S. Senate race it has spent its money on ads opposing Democrat Mary Peltola.

C00876482.about: Retire Career Politicians is a Washington-based super PAC that backed independent Dan Osborn's 2024 challenge to Republican Sen. Deb Fischer in Nebraska. Its treasurer is Christopher Koob, a former Democratic National Committee and Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee staffer, and its funders included Senate Majority PAC, the LCV Victory Fund, the Sixteen Thirty Fund, Movement Voter Project, and donor Donald Sussman. Nearly all of its spending went to TV and digital ads supporting Osborn and attacking Fischer.

C00879510.about: America PAC is a super PAC founded by Elon Musk in 2024, who supplies the great majority of its money; other backers include Doug Leone, Joe Lonsdale and Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss. It financed door-to-door canvassing, voter petitions and social media ads for Donald Trump in 2024. In the 2026 midterms it spent to help Republicans in Senate and House races, most heavily in Texas against Democrat James Talarico.

C00886614.about: Your Community PAC is a Democratic-aligned super PAC registered in Wilmington, Delaware. Its money comes mainly from large progressive nonprofit and political groups, led by the Sixteen Thirty Fund, the North Fund, American Opportunity Action, the Center for Voter Information, United Futures and the Green Advocacy Project. In 2024 it backed Kamala Harris with billboards, mail and canvassing, and in 2026 it has run television ads against Republican House members including Max Miller of Ohio and Brad Finstad of Minnesota.

C00894709.about: Pine Tree Results PAC is a Republican super PAC formed in early 2025 to support Sen. Susan Collins of Maine in her 2026 reelection. Its largest donor is Stronger America Inc., a Virginia-based nonprofit led by Republican operative Paul Cooksey, and other major backers include Blackstone CEO Stephen Schwarzman, New Balance chairman Jim Davis, hedge fund manager Paul Singer and Palantir CEO Alex Karp. It runs TV and online ads attacking Collins's Democratic opponents, first Graham Platner and then nominee Troy Jackson.

C00896365.about: Keep America Great PAC is a Republican super PAC formed in 2025 to help Rep. Andy Barr win Kentucky's open U.S. Senate seat, and its filings list Barr's campaign committee as a connected organization. Its largest donors include Foris DAX, the company behind Crypto.com, and the American Jobs and Growth Fund. It spent millions on TV ads in the 2026 Republican primary, much of it attacking rival Nate Morris and his company's immigration record.

C00898130.about: Fight for Kentucky is the super PAC backing businessman Nate Morris in Kentucky's 2026 Republican Senate primary. Its biggest donors include Elon Musk, investor Thomas Klingenstein and the conservative super PAC Jefferson Rising. It spent heavily on broadcast and connected-TV ads promoting Morris and attacking his primary rival, Rep. Andy Barr.

C00901223.about: Lone Star Liberty PAC is a super PAC formed to back Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton's 2026 Republican campaign for the U.S. Senate. Its donors include Midland oilman Douglas Scharbauer, Curves founder Gary Heavin and Preserve Texas Inc., a Virginia-based nonprofit formed shortly after Paxton entered the race. It hosted rallies for Paxton and ran TV ads attacking Sen. John Cornyn in the primary and runoff, including buys in South Florida aimed at President Trump at Mar-a-Lago, and also spent against Rep. Wesley Hunt and Democratic nominee James Talarico.

C00902320.about: Illinois Future PAC is a super PAC formed in 2025 to back Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton in Illinois's 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate. Gov. JB Pritzker was its main funder, with other large gifts from members of the Pritzker family and Chicago Cubs co-owner Laura Ricketts. It ran broadcast ads promoting Stratton and attacking her primary rival, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi.

C00904730.about: Land I Love PAC is a Republican super PAC registered in Mountain Brook, Alabama, in 2025, funded almost entirely by the Congressional Leadership Fund, the House Republican leadership's super PAC. It backed Jimmy Patronis in Florida's 2025 special House election and in 2026 ran media against Democrat Rebecca Bennett in New Jersey's 7th District race against Rep. Tom Kean Jr.

C00906263.about: The Louisiana Freedom Fund is a super PAC formed in 2025 to support Republican Senator Bill Cassidy's 2026 renomination bid. Its filings list Cassidy Leadership Fund as a joint fundraising representative, and its main funders are Louisiana Legacy Policy Solutions, Louisiana Legacy PAC and Conservative Values for Louisiana. It spent heavily on television ads attacking Cassidy's primary challenger, Representative Julia Letlow, casting her as a liberal who voted with Joe Biden.

C00906701.about: America First Agriculture Action is a super PAC registered in 2025 that shares a treasurer, Charles Gantt, with President Trump's super PAC MAGA Inc. Its largest donors are cannabis companies, including Trulieve, Curaleaf, Verano and Ascend Wellness. It spends on direct mail and digital ads promoting vulnerable House Republicans such as Bryan Steil, Nick Begich, Rob Bresnahan, Juan Ciscomani and Ryan Mackenzie, and has also run ads praising Trump's move to reschedule marijuana.

C00908707.about: BDA PAC, known as Blue Dog Action, is the outside-spending group the Blue Dog Coalition of fiscally conservative House Democrats set up in 2025 to back its candidates in Democratic primaries; it is separate from the coalition's Blue Dog PAC, which gives directly to candidates. It was co-founded by Phil Gardner, a senior adviser to Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, and its donors include the nonprofits Opportunity Forward Alliance and The Bench, Blue Dog Action Fund, and Walmart heir Sam Walton. It runs TV and media ads, including for Rep. Mike Thompson in his same-party California general election, for Bobby Pulido in Texas and for Bale Dalton in Florida.

C00908723.about: MAGA KY is a super PAC formed by Donald Trump's campaign advisers in 2025 to defeat Rep. Thomas Massie in Kentucky's Republican primary. Its money came mainly from hedge fund manager Paul Singer, directly and through America 21 PAC, with further support from Miriam Adelson, investor John Paulson and MAGA Inc. It ran TV ads attacking Massie for nearly a year and promoted Trump-endorsed challenger Ed Gallrein, who beat Massie in the May 2026 primary.

C00911610.about: Digital Freedom Fund is a pro-cryptocurrency super PAC launched in 2025 by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, the founders of the Gemini exchange, who seeded it with about $21 million in bitcoin; Gemini Trust Company is also a major donor. It works to elect Republicans and defeat Democrats who oppose the crypto industry's agenda, chiefly through direct mail and text messages, such as backing Jon Husted and opposing Sherrod Brown in Ohio's Senate race.

C00912865.about: Ohio Flyer PAC is a Republican super PAC devoted to electing Jon Husted to the U.S. Senate from Ohio; its FEC filings list Husted's committee Team Husted as an affiliated organization, and Team Husted has transferred money to it. Its largest donors include Preserving the Republic's Promise, the Ohio group A Public Voice, Beemok founder Ben Navarro, Brian Colleran of Foundations Health Solutions, and Chevron. It spends on TV, streaming and digital ads and direct mail attacking Democrat Sherrod Brown.

C00916692.about: American Mission is the Republican-facing super PAC of Leading the Future, the artificial intelligence industry's political network launched in 2025 and bankrolled by venture capitalists Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, OpenAI president Greg Brockman, and Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale.
