Funded by transfers from Leading the Future, it spends in Republican primaries on ads that focus on issues like Trump and immigration rather than AI, backing candidates such as Chris Gober in Texas and Clay Fuller and Jim Kingston in Georgia. Its Democratic counterpart is Think Big.

C00918268.about: Lone Star Rising PAC is a Democratic super PAC formed in Texas in 2025 to support James Talarico's campaign for the U.S. Senate. It is directed by longtime Democratic operative Garry Jones, with Talarico's former Teach for America colleague Alex Clark as treasurer, and its largest backers include Government That Works PAC, LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, and investors Stephen Mandel and Mark Heising. It spent most of its money on TV ads promoting Talarico and attacking U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett in the 2026 Democratic Senate primary, and has also backed Texas House Democrats.

C00923417.about: Think Big is the Democratic-facing super PAC of Leading the Future, the artificial intelligence industry's political network launched in 2025 and bankrolled by venture capitalists Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, OpenAI president Greg Brockman, and Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale. Funded by transfers from Leading the Future, it spends in Democratic primaries for candidates such as Ben McAdams in Utah and Ritchie Torres in New York, and ran ads opposing Alex Bores in New York. Its ads center on issues like opposition to Trump rather than AI; its Republican counterpart is American Mission.

C00932707.about: Conservative Texans PAC is a super PAC formed in early 2026 to spend in Texas' Republican U.S. Senate primary on behalf of Sen. John Cornyn. All of its money came from another super PAC, Conservative Americans PAC, whose largest funder is the American Prosperity Alliance. It ran TV ads attacking Rep. Wesley Hunt as a disloyal Republican.

C00932723.about: American Priorities is a pro-Palestine super PAC formed in February 2026 to counter the influence of AIPAC and other pro-Israel groups in Democratic primaries. Its donors include tech executives such as Omer Hasan and Outschool founder Amir Nathoo, Texas businessman Hussein Mahrouq and Justice Democrats. It runs TV and digital ads for progressive challengers, including Adam Hamawy in New Jersey, Darializa Avila Chevalier in New York, Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania and Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, often against incumbents backed by pro-Israel groups.

C00935049.about: Affordable Chicago Now! is a super PAC formed ahead of the March 2026 Democratic primary in Illinois's 2nd Congressional District, where it ran advertising backing Cook County Commissioner and former Illinois Planned Parenthood chair Donna Miller. FEC filings released after the primary showed it was bankrolled by the United Democracy Project, the super PAC affiliated with the pro-Israel lobby AIPAC.

C00935973.about: North Star Dawn PAC is a super PAC that backed Rep. Angie Craig in Minnesota's 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate. Its money came from the Civic Progress Fund, a nonprofit that does not disclose its donors. It ran TV ads promoting Craig and attacking her primary opponent, Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, including one that used an AI-generated image of Flanagan.

C00936591.about: Stand for New York PAC is a super PAC formed in 2026 and funded almost entirely by former New York City mayor Michael Bloomberg. It backed Micah Lasher, a former Bloomberg aide endorsed by retiring Representative Jerry Nadler, in the Democratic primary for New York's 12th District in Manhattan, paying for TV, mail and digital advertising.

C00936724.about: Elect Chicago Women is a super PAC formed in January 2026 to spend in Chicago-area Democratic House primaries. It ran TV ads backing former Rep. Melissa Bean in Illinois' 8th District and state Sen. Laura Fine in the 9th District, and spent against Evanston Mayor Daniel Biss in the 9th District race.

C00940957.about: Accountability Project Inc. is a New Orleans-based super PAC that has spent exclusively to support U.S. Rep. Julia Letlow's 2026 Republican campaign for the U.S. Senate in Louisiana, in which she challenged Sen. Bill Cassidy. Its largest funder is Hope in Action PAC, a Letlow-aligned super PAC, which sent it roughly $2.9 million. Its money has gone to independent ads in the Senate primary and runoff.

C00943753.about: Kentucky 4th PAC is a super PAC formed in March 2026 to defend Rep. Thomas Massie in his Republican primary in Kentucky's 4th District. It spent nearly all of its money on ads attacking Trump-endorsed challenger Ed Gallrein in the final weeks before the May 2026 primary, which Gallrein won. Nearly all of its funding came from Tamarack Aspen Inc., a Delaware nonprofit created shortly before the race, and the Campaign Legal Center has filed FEC complaints over its reporting and funding.

C00949248.about: Pro-Choice Majority Action is a super PAC formed in May 2026 and linked to Elect Democratic Women, whose action fund supplied nearly all of its early money after receiving funds from the AIPAC-affiliated United Democracy Project. It spends in Democratic House primaries, most heavily on television ads backing Rep. Diana DeGette of Colorado and attacking her challenger Melat Kiros.

C00952259.about: A Stronger Michigan is a super PAC formed in June 2026 to back Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic primary for an open U.S. Senate seat. Nearly all of its money came from Center Forward, a nonprofit advocacy group whose known donors include PhRMA, PG&E, the Biotechnology Innovation Organization and the Business Roundtable. It spent on a run of ads promoting Stevens in her primary against Abdul El-Sayed.

C00953299.about: People Over Politics Action Fund is a Kansas super PAC formed to oppose Republican Sen. Roger Marshall in his 2026 reelection race. It spends on broadcast television advertising, including ads attacking Marshall over his role in blocking the release of files related to Jeffrey Epstein.

C00953398.about: The Georgia Way is a super PAC affiliated with Senate Majority PAC, the main outside group of Senate Democrats, and shares its treasurer, Rebecca Lambe. Registered in June 2026, it is funded through transfers from its affiliated committee. It runs ads in Georgia's 2026 Senate race supporting Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff and attacking Republican nominee Mike Collins.

C00956292.about: Nebraska Values PAC is a super PAC backing independent Dan Osborn in Nebraska's 2026 U.S. Senate race. It spends mainly on television advertising attacking Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts, including a 60-second spot criticizing Ricketts over a pardon he supported as governor.

C00957522.about: North Star is a Democratic super PAC registered in July 2026 to oppose Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race against Democrat Mary Peltola. It is funded almost entirely by Senate Majority PAC, the main super PAC working to elect Democratic senators. It is the largest outside spender on Peltola's side, buying TV and digital ads that tie Sullivan to commercial trawling interests blamed for falling salmon runs and to cuts in Medicaid and health subsidies.

C00960211.about: Texas PAC is a Republican super PAC connected to Senate Leadership Fund, the main super PAC of Senate Republican leadership, set up for the 2026 Texas U.S. Senate race. It runs broadcast television ads in the Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, San Antonio and Austin markets attacking Democratic nominee James Talarico and promoting Republican Ken Paxton.

C00960435.about: No Going Back PAC is a Republican super PAC formed in September 2026 and financed by MAGA Inc., the main super PAC aligned with President Donald Trump, with which it shares a treasurer and address. It spends almost entirely on attack ads against Democratic candidates in competitive Senate and House races, including Sherrod Brown in Ohio, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Roy Cooper in North Carolina, along with ads supporting Republicans such as Jon Husted and Dan Sullivan.

C00960443.about: Safety & Affordability PAC is a Trump-aligned Republican super PAC formed in September 2026 and funded almost entirely by MAGA Inc., the main pro-Trump super PAC. It shares its treasurer with No Going Back PAC, a sister group focused on Senate races, while this PAC concentrates on House races. It buys TV and connected-TV ads attacking Democratic House candidates in battleground districts and backing Republicans such as Mike Lawler and Juan Ciscomani.

C00961276.about: Lower Costs Now is a Democratic super PAC formed in September 2026 and affiliated with FF PAC, the group formerly known as Future Forward USA PAC. Nearly all of its money came as transfers from Senate Majority PAC and FF PAC. It runs TV and online ads in Senate races, backing Democrats such as Jon Ossoff, James Talarico and Josh Turek and attacking Republicans including Mike Collins, Jon Husted and Roger Marshall, with Iowa its biggest target.

C00961342.about: The Maine Standard is a Republican super PAC formed in September 2026 to oppose Democrat Troy Jackson in Maine's U.S. Senate race. It is funded by the Senate Leadership Fund, the leading super PAC working to elect Republicans to the Senate, and spends its money on media buys attacking Jackson.

C90011156.about: Working America is the community affiliate of the AFL-CIO, the national federation of labor unions, built to organize working people who do not belong to a union. It runs a large paid door-to-door canvassing operation in battleground states such as Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, persuading working-class voters to back Democratic candidates. Its independent spending has supported Democratic Senate candidates including Raphael Warnock, John Fetterman and Sherrod Brown.

C90011172.about: The AFSCME Working Families Fund is the independent-expenditure fund of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees, the union of public-sector workers. It spends on TV ads, direct mail, digital ads, phone calls and door-to-door canvassing to support Democratic House and Senate candidates and oppose Republicans.
